summary: A framework from SRI-ARC for coordinating the surveys and data-gathering efforts about network resources, the Resource Notebook. The goals were to avoid swamping sites with overlapping questionnaires and to make the NIC responsible for coordination. ARPA had agreed to the scheme.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 464 proposes one coordinated process for gathering information about network resources. Regional collectors would send site information to the NIC, which would check and share it.

questions: what was the nic's role in the arpanet
subtitle: A framework for coordinating the collection and sharing of network resource information.

tldr.problem: Many separate surveys about Resource Notebook information could overwhelm the sites and people asked to supply it.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC assigns coordination of collection, checking and distribution to the NIC, with regional collectors helping gather information from sites.
tldr.outcome: The framework had ARPA's agreement, but this RFC presents it as a proposal and requests discussion. The text does not report what followed.

today: The unit records RFC 464's status as Unknown and lists no updates or obsoleting RFCs. The document is a historical framework proposal for coordinating resource information.

sections.title: Why Coordinate the Surveys
sections.content:
The RFC offers a framework for coordinating surveys and data gathering about Resource Notebook information. It says ARPA had agreed to the framework.

The plan has two goals: avoid multiplying data-gathering efforts that could overwhelm contributors, and make the NIC responsible for coordinating Resource Notebook work. Two companion NIC documents cover the notebook's history and the questionnaire then being sent to server sites.
sections.plainLanguage: The proposal aims to avoid asking the same sites for the same information through many separate surveys. It puts one coordinating role with the NIC.

sections.title: Collecting and Checking Information
sections.content:
The NIC would coordinate collection, verification and distribution of resource information. Regional data collectors would help the NIC and the sites supplying information. The RFC suggests starting with five regions: Boston, Washington DC, San Francisco, Los Angeles and Mid-Continent.

A regional agent would collect information from sites in that region and send it to the NIC's Resource Notebook database. The NIC would work with the regional agents to keep the information accurate and up to date.
sections.plainLanguage: Regional collectors gather information from nearby sites and pass it to the NIC. The NIC works with them to check and maintain the shared information.

sections.title: Sharing Views and Reviewing the Plan
sections.content:
The RFC says different groups may prepare different subsets, or “views,” of the full Resource Notebook database. These views should be available online at the NIC and offline, regardless of which groups prepare them.

A working group of people interested in the Resource Notebook would meet periodically to review the situation and propose improvements. The author invites comments and suggests a meeting at SRI-ARC; the document gives a proposed date and asks for comments by an earlier date.
sections.plainLanguage: People could receive a complete database or a selected view of it, online or offline. A working group would review needs and suggest improvements.

references.text: Iseli, J. and Crocker, D., Responding to User Needs, NWG/RFC 462, NIC 14434.
